body.statement: For \(\mathsf E_5\), both displayed models have \(P(X=x,Z=z,Y=y)=1/8\) for all \(x,z,y\in\{0,1\}\), while \(P_{X=0}^{\rho^+_5}(Y=1)=1/2\) and \(P_{X=0}^{\rho^-_5}(Y=1)=97/200\), giving the exact gap \(3/200\). Deleting the active edge \(T\to Z\) leaves the front-door graph \(X\to Z\to Y\) with \(X\leftrightarrow Y\), which has no hedge, whereas the empty trace retains \(F=\{Y\}\subset F'=\{X,Z,Y\}\) and the displayed difference of outcome rows lies in the corresponding observed kernel. For \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{bow}}\), the reference context gives \(P_{X=0}(Y=1)=4P(A=0,X=0,Y=1)=2/5\) and \(P_{X=1}(Y=1)=4P(A=0,X=1,Y=1)=3/5\). Thus the two query coefficient vectors lie in the row space of the full observed-cell matrix, so \(\mathsf{Verify}_{\mathrm{sink}}\) structurally rejects the local \(A=1\) bow forest before any countermodel is formed.
body.justification: The exact pair tests both required boundaries: active pruning can erase the obstruction, while a reference context can annihilate a local forest through row-space gluing.
body.gap: Chen and Darwiche give a qualitative pruning warning; these rational fixtures impose two-child latents, positivity, an exact \(3/200\) gap, and structural reference-context rejection.
body.consumer: The tables are deterministic fixtures for \(Y_0\)'s trace retention, rational contraction, and row-space rejection logic.
body.proof_tex:
Write probabilities in the five-node instance of \(\texttt{def:five-node-rational-instance}\) under either model as \(P\), except when the superscript distinguishing \(\rho _5^+\) and \(\rho _5^-\) is needed.  Put
\[
 a_u=P(X=0\mid U=u),\qquad
 g_{xt}=P(Z=0\mid X=x,T=t).
\]
The displayed tables in that definition give
\[
 (a_0,a_1)=\left(\frac34,\frac14\right),\qquad
 g_{00}=g_{01}=\frac12,\qquad
 (g_{10},g_{11})=\left(\frac34,\frac14\right).
\]
Because \(U\) and \(T\) are independent and fair, for either \(z\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(X=0,Z=z)
 &=\frac14\sum_{u=0}^1 a_u\sum_{t=0}^1
       P(Z=z\mid X=0,T=t)\\
 &=\frac14\left(\frac34+\frac14\right)
       \left(\frac12+\frac12\right)=\frac14.
 \end{aligned}
\]
For \(z=0\), the corresponding calculation at \(X=1\) is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(X=1,Z=0)
 &=\frac14\sum_{u=0}^1(1-a_u)\sum_{t=0}^1g_{1t}\\
 &=\frac14\left(\frac14+\frac34\right)
       \left(\frac34+\frac14\right)=\frac14,
 \end{aligned}
\]
and replacing every \(g_{1t}\) by \(1-g_{1t}\) gives \(P(X=1,Z=1)=1/4\).  Thus \((X,Z)\) is uniform in both models.  Every outcome row of \(\rho _5^+\) is \(1/2\), so
\[
 P_{\rho _5^+}(X=x,Z=z,Y=y)=\frac14\frac12=\frac18
 \quad\text{for all }(x,z,y)\in\{0,1\}^3.
\]

It remains to verify that changing the four displayed \(Z=0\) outcome rows does not alter this observed table.  Define their changes, in the order \((u,t)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), by
\[
 \Delta=(\Delta_{00},\Delta_{01},\Delta_{10},\Delta_{11})
 =\frac1{100}(3,3,7,-25).
\]
For the observed cell \((X,Z,Y)=(0,0,1)\), the four latent weights are \((3,3,1,1)/32\).  Hence its increment is
\[
 \frac1{32}(3,3,1,1)\Delta^{\mathsf T}
 =\frac{9+9+7-25}{3200}=0.
\]
For the cell \((X,Z,Y)=(1,0,1)\), the four latent weights are \((3,1,9,3)/64\), and its increment is
\[
 \frac1{64}(3,1,9,3)\Delta^{\mathsf T}
 =\frac{9+3+63-75}{6400}=0.
\]
The outcome rows with \(Z=1\) are unchanged, so the increments of the two remaining observed \(Y=1\) cells are also zero.  The preceding uniformity calculation fixes every \((X,Z)\)-marginal at \(1/4\); binary complementation therefore makes every \(Y=0\) cell agree as well.  Consequently
\[
 P_{\rho _5^-}(X=x,Z=z,Y=y)
 =P_{\rho _5^+}(X=x,Z=z,Y=y)=\frac18
\]
for every observed assignment.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\), the truncated factorization leaves \(U\) and \(T\) independent and fair, and the CSI row gives \(P(Z=0\mid X=0,T=t)=1/2\) for each \(t\).  The positive model has constant outcome probability \(1/2\), whereas the query increment in the negative model is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{X=0}^{\rho _5^-}(Y=1)-P_{X=0}^{\rho _5^+}(Y=1)
 &=\sum_{u,t}\frac14\frac12\Delta_{ut}\\
 &=\frac18\frac{3+3+7-25}{100}=-\frac3{200}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(P_{X=0}^{\rho _5^+}(Y=1)=1/2\) and \(P_{X=0}^{\rho _5^-}(Y=1)=97/200\), proving the stated gap.  Every listed primitive probability and its binary complement lies strictly between zero and one.  The only CSI equality is the equality of the two \(Z\)-rows at \(X=0\), which is explicit above; all root laws are normalized and \(U,T\) are independent.  Hence both tables are positive quotient-shared models.  Notice also that the activation variable is the observed vertex \(X\), while \(U\to X\); thus \(X\) is not a root.  This admissible instance is therefore a strict input-syntax witness beyond the subclass in which every observed activation variable must be a root.

We next verify the trace boundary using \(\texttt{def:rooted-forest-obstruction}\).  At the active \(X=0\) context, deletion of \(T\to Z\) removes the latent common cause of \(Z\) and \(Y\).  The observed latent projection then has directed edges \(X\to Z\to Y\) and the sole bidirected edge \(X\leftrightarrow Y\).  A one-district C-forest meeting the treatment vertex \(X\) can contain no \(Z\), since \(Z\) has no incident bidirected edge.  Its vertex set is therefore either \(\{X\}\) or \(\{X,Y\}\).  In the first case its childless set is \(\{X\}\).  In the second case there is no directed edge between \(X\) and \(Y\) in the induced forest, so its childless set is \(\{X,Y\}\).  Both possibilities contain \(X\), while
\[
 X\notin\operatorname{An}_{H_{k,t}\setminus X}(Y).
\]
They therefore violate the required condition \(R_0\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{H_{k,t}\setminus X}(Y)\).  No rooted C-forest obstruction pair exists after the active deletion.

For the empty trace, retain the original latent projection and take
\[
 F=\{Y\}\subset F'=\{X,Z,Y\}.
\]
The bidirected edges \(X\leftrightarrow Y\) and \(Z\leftrightarrow Y\) make \(F'\) a single district.  Choosing the directed forest edges \(X\to Z\to Y\) gives each vertex at most one directed child, and both \(F\) and \(F'\) have childless set \(R_0=\{Y\}\).  Moreover,
\[
 F\cap X=\varnothing,\qquad F'\cap X\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad \{Y\}\subseteq\operatorname{An}_{H_{k,t}\setminus X}(Y),
\]
where ancestry is reflexive.  Hence this is a rooted C-forest pair under \(\texttt{def:rooted-forest-obstruction}\).

Extend \(\Delta\) to the vector \(\delta\) of outcome-row coordinates by putting \(\delta_{ut0}=\Delta_{ut}\) and \(\delta_{ut1}=0\).  The only CSI concerns the child \(Z\), so the four altered complete parent rows of \(Y\) remain distinct quotient coordinates; inspection of the retained pair shows that they are among its exposed sink-row classes.  Thus \(\delta\) is supported on \(J_{t,F}\).  The four observed-cell calculations above, together with binary complementation, are exactly the full structural contraction equations
\[
 A_{\eta,t,F}\delta=0.
\]
The intervention calculation is the corresponding query contraction,
\[
 b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\delta=-\frac3{200}\ne0.
\]
Therefore the displayed row difference belongs to the observed kernel but changes the causal query.  Equivalently, \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\) cannot lie in \(\operatorname{row}(A_{\eta,t,F})\); otherwise \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_{\eta,t,F}\) would imply \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\delta=0\).  The non-row-space branch of \(\texttt{lem:forest-to-kernel-lift}\) consequently yields the verifier's canonical forest-supported null vector, and \(\texttt{thm:binary-sink-certificate-soundness}\) supplies the associated positive shared-row countermodel interpretation.

Finally consider \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{bow}}\) from \(\texttt{def:reference-context-bow-instance}\).  Since \(A\) and \(U\) are independent and fair and the \(A=0\) CSI makes \(P(X=x\mid A=0,U=u)=1/2\), Bayes' rule has the positive denominator
\[
 P(A=0,X=x)=\sum_u\frac12\frac12\frac12=\frac14
\]
and gives \(P(U=u\mid A=0,X=x)=1/2\).  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{X=0}(Y=1)&=\frac12\left(\frac15+\frac35\right)=\frac25,\\
 P_{X=1}(Y=1)&=\frac12\left(\frac25+\frac45\right)=\frac35.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The same mixtures occur in the observed reference context, so
\[
 P_{X=x}(Y=1)=4P(A=0,X=x,Y=1),\qquad x\in\{0,1\}.
\]
In particular the displayed cells give \(4(1/10)=2/5\) and \(4(3/20)=3/5\), as asserted.

For the exact row-space check, order the outcome-row coordinates as
\[
 p=(p_{00},p_{01},p_{10},p_{11})^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad p_{xu}=P(Y=1\mid X=x,U=u).
\]
The two intervention coefficient rows are
\[
 b_0^{\mathsf T}=\left(\frac12,\frac12,0,0\right),
 \qquad
 b_1^{\mathsf T}=\left(0,0,\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]
The observed \(Y=1\) cell in the reference context has contraction
\[
 P(A=0,X=x,Y=1)=\sum_u\frac12\frac12\frac12p_{xu}.
\]
Accordingly, the full observed-cell coefficient matrix has, at rows \((A,X,Y)=(0,0,1)\) and \((0,1,1)\), respectively,
\[
 r_0^{\mathsf T}=\frac14 b_0^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad r_1^{\mathsf T}=\frac14 b_1^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus \(b_x^{\mathsf T}=4r_x^{\mathsf T}\) belongs to the observed row space for each \(x\).  This relation survives the forest restriction in \(\texttt{def:fixed-sink-linearization}\): both sides are projected onto \(J_{t,F}\), and \(b_x\) is supported on the queried \(X=x\) outcome rows.  Hence \(b_{\eta,t,F}^{\mathsf T}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\eta,t,F})\) for the purported local \(A=1\) bow forest.  The row-space alternative in \(\texttt{lem:forest-to-kernel-lift}\), equivalently the explicit rejection test in \(\texttt{def:binary-sink-verifier}\), therefore rejects that forest before constructing a countermodel.  This completes every assertion of the proposition.
